title: identity_claim is EMPTY: D4 is structurally unanswerable
evidence: GQ-010-BASELINE.html §4.1. identity_claim = 0 rows. merged_into non-null = 0. state='merged' = 0.

spec.description: The recorded defect PG-AUDIT-002/PGRT-004 says 'ask.py never reads identity_claim', which implies claims exist and are ignored. The truth is worse: there are NO CLAIMS TO IGNORE. Both halves are broken - ask.py contains no reference to identity_claim across all 357 lines, AND the table holds zero rows. This makes TASK-0002 (Lane 6) NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT: wiring ask.py to read the table changes nothing until something writes to it.
spec.context: The README calls identity claims its central safety design: 'Every proposed match is a row in identity_claim with a method, a confidence and the literal evidence.' The table exists, is correctly designed, is indexed on status, and is empty. Live consequence: ask.py --who 'Spinoza' returns 'baruch-spinoza' (registry) and 'bk:spinoza, benedictus de|1632-1677' (books) as two unrelated matches. They are the same human. The graph ranks neither, proposes no claim, and offers no adjudication path. One point in its favour: the John Murray fusion disaster has NOT happened - but that safety is accidental, holding because the matcher never ran, not because a guard prevented it. 31 (platform,value) pairs map to multiple people and 1,266 names are shared across rows, so the blast radius is latent, not absent. Measured 2026-08-07 by PG-BASELINE against the shipped graph-v2 asset: people_graph_v2.sqlite, 1,113,350,144 bytes, db SHA-256 9938237a33277fe3a29a278d68c361a1f300d9060740cc2e917920157d9b919b, at repo commit de048bb3b34bf931b56fd741cb46c1334acdfb98.
